EN Revision Imported Date: 11/10/2026

EN Revision Text: PART 21 - NON-COMPLIANT ELECTROMECHANICAL RELAYS

The following is a summary of information was provided by ABB Inc. via email:

On July 17, 2026, during calibration of a KF relay, ABB identified a deviation from the specified coil-assembly drying process. The affected coil assembly had completed the required air-drying stage, however, the subsequent force-drying (baking) stage had not been performed. The applicable process specifications required dipped transformers and coil assemblies to undergo a defined air-drying period followed by the specified force-drying (baking) cycle. After a review of production records, ABB identified 60 relays potentially manufactured under this condition and supplied to 12 customers. The affected population includes multiple class 1E electromechanical relay styles. Engineering testing of representative assemblies manufactured under the evaluated process conditions demonstrated compliance with the applicable 2.2 kV hi-pot acceptance criteria, and no immediate dielectric failure conditions were attributable to omission of the force-drying step that was identified under the tested dry condition. As of the date of this notification, ABB has not received any in-service failure reports from customers associated with the affected relays that are attributable to this deviation.

Affected Customers:
Catawba Nuclear Station
Oconee Nuclear Station
Georgia Power
Entergy Louisiana LLC
PSEG Nuclear LLC
Exelon Business Services
Westinghouse Electric
Duke Energy Carolinas
Dominion Energy Virginia
Constellation Energy Generation
Nextera Energy Resources

AGREEMENT STATE REPORT - MEDICAL EVENT

The following is a summary of information provided by the Minnesota Department of Health via email:

On November 2, 2026, the licensee reported that a patient had an underdose during a Y-90 TheraSphere treatment. No dose was delivered to patient and all activity remained in the vial and tubing. The activity in the vial and tubing pretreatment and posttreatment was 1.78 GBq and 1.74 GBq, respectively. The patient was surveyed after the procedure with no radiation detected. The patient also had a post treatment SPECT which showed no activity. The licensee's procedures were followed. The licensee is working with the manufacturer to determine what might have happened.

Minnesota Event Report ID Number: MN260001

A Medical Event may indicate potential problems in a medical facility's use of radioactive materials. It does not necessarily result in harm to the patient.

AGREEMENT STATE REPORT - LOST SOURCES

The following information was provided by the Ohio Department of Health, Bureau of Environmental Health and Radiation Protection (the Department), via email:

"After performing an onsite inspection, an inspector determined that the licensee had potentially lost two standard cesium-137 calibration sources. The two sources were a rod source containing 0.5 microcuries of Cs-137, serial number 1113-11-40, dated 5/1/2005, and a vial source containing 205.5 microcuries of Cs-137, serial number 76910, dated 3/1/2006. The licensee is a private cardiovascular physician's office which has not performed nuclear procedures for four years. During the inspection, the licensee could not account for the two calibration sources that were listed on their last sealed source inventory record, which was outdated by a few years. The licensee was given 24 hours to account for the sources in case they were transferred or found post inspection. The licensee failed to update the status of the sources and the Department has determined the sources were lost. The results of this inspection and potential findings are still pending. This event will remain open until the inspection is closed."

Ohio incident number: OH260008

THIS MATERIAL EVENT CONTAINS A 'Less than Cat 3' LEVEL OF RADIOACTIVE MATERIAL

Sources that are "Less than IAEA Category 3 sources," are either sources that are very unlikely to cause permanent injury to individuals or contain a very small amount of radioactive material that would not cause any permanent injury. Some of these sources, such as moisture density gauges or thickness gauges that are Category 4, the amount of unshielded radioactive material, if not safely managed or securely protected, could possibly - although it is unlikely - temporarily injure someone who handled it or were otherwise in contact with it, or who were close to it for a period of many weeks. For additional information go to http://www-pub.iaea.org/MTCD/publications/PDF/Pub1227_web.pdf
